topics.title: US tightens pressure on Iran
topics.summary: The U.S. added new sanctions aimed at Iran-linked financial networks while regional tensions and oil-route concerns continued to weigh on diplomacy and markets.
topics.discussionPrompt: When pressure keeps building from every side, who in the studio would try diplomacy first and who would make it worse?

topics.title: Strong jobs report rattles markets
topics.summary: U.S. stocks slipped after August hiring came in stronger than expected, raising investor bets that the Federal Reserve may keep rates higher to fight inflation.
topics.discussionPrompt: If good news makes everyone nervous, how do you decide whether to celebrate or start checking the budget?

topics.title: Kyiv faces more daytime attacks
topics.summary: Russia's drone and missile strikes on Kyiv are increasingly disrupting daytime routines, adding pressure to commutes, schools, public services, and daily civilian life.
topics.discussionPrompt: When interruptions stop being rare and become routine, what helps people keep a normal day going?

topics.title: Ukraine peace diplomacy stirs again
topics.summary: U.S. negotiators are expected to visit Kyiv and Moscow as leaders signal possible openings for talks, even as fighting and drone strikes continue.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a peace talk feel serious: who shows up, what they offer, or whether the noise quiets down?

topics.title: Nepal flood rescue brings relief
topics.summary: Rescuers pulled two trapped workers from a hydropower tunnel nine days after severe Nepal floods, while the disaster kept attention on mountain-region warning systems.
topics.discussionPrompt: What kind of survival story would make the whole studio go quiet for a second, then ask a hundred questions?

topics.title: Hollywood summer rebounds
topics.summary: The summer box office had its strongest showing in years, helped by younger audiences, premium screens, familiar franchises, and several original breakout films.
topics.discussionPrompt: What gets people off the couch for a movie now: spectacle, nostalgia, friends, or just needing a night out?

topics.title: Quirky science wins Ig Nobels
topics.summary: This year's Ig Nobel prizes highlighted oddball research, including studies tied to unusual animal biology and everyday habits, celebrating science that makes people laugh and think.
topics.discussionPrompt: What ridiculous question would secretly deserve a proper experiment in the studio?

topics.title: Australia debates skilled migration
topics.summary: Australian leaders and unions debated how skilled migration, AI, trades shortages, and worker protections should fit together as the country plans for future labor needs.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a workplace suddenly needs totally new skills, should it hire, retrain, or slow down and rethink the whole plan?

topics.title: Malta verdict alarms journalists
topics.summary: The acquittal of Yorgen Fenech in the Daphne Caruana Galizia case renewed concern about journalist safety, accountability, and press freedom in Europe.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a verdict leaves people uneasy, what should happen next: appeal, reform, public pressure, or all of it?

topics.title: Mail-voting fight reaches court again
topics.summary: The Trump administration asked the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene over blocked USPS mail-voting restrictions as states prepare ballots for the midterm elections.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an election rule changes right before voting starts, what would make people trust the process?
